guidance: Read the torque at the bit wherever a downhole tool measures it: surface torque includes the drag of the whole drill string and inflates the figure. Compare runs in the same hole size, bit type and formation, and average the penetration rate over a steady interval rather than reading it at one instant, because the rotary term divides by that rate.
method: Mechanical specific energy is the mechanical work a bit spends to destroy a unit volume of rock. Teale's equation adds an axial and a rotary term: MSE = WOB / Ab + 120π · RPM · T / (Ab · ROP), where Ab is the bit face area, π D² / 4, WOB the weight on bit, T the torque at the bit, RPM the rotary speed and ROP the rate of penetration. The constant 120π reconciles the oilfield units (lbf, ft·lbf, in², rev/min, ft/h) to psi; once those unit conversions are applied it carries no dimension, so the same form gives pascals from newtons, newton-metres, square metres, rev/min and metres per hour. This page converts every entry to SI, computes Ab = π D² / 4, the axial term WOB / Ab and the rotary term 2π (RPM / 60) T / (Ab · ROP), sums them and reports MPa and psi. The two shares are each term over the total, so they add to 100. Worked default: 80 kN, 3 kN·m, 120 rpm and 25 m/h on a 215.9 mm bit give a face area of 366.1 cm², a weight term of 2.19 MPa, a rotary term of 148.29 MPa and 150.47 MPa (21,824 psi) in total, 98.5 percent of it rotary. Inputs are limited to a weight on bit of 0 to 2,000 kN (0 to 450,000 lbf), a torque of 0 to 200 kN·m (0 to 150,000 ft·lbf), a rotary speed of 0 to 1,000 rpm, a rate of penetration of 0.1 to 1,000 m/h (0.3 to 3,280 ft/h) and a bit diameter of 10 to 1,500 mm (0.4 to 59 in); a rate of zero or a diameter of zero is refused because the energy would be undefined or unbounded. The page reduces one interval: it assumes the torque and the penetration rate describe the same steady interval at the same hole size, treats the bit as a flat face of the nominal diameter, and does not model bit wear, bit balling, vibration, nozzle hydraulics, the drag of the drill string above the bit or the strength of the rock. Surface torque inflates the figure because it carries that drag, so a downhole torque measurement is preferable. The number is a monitoring and comparison figure for one bit and one hole size, not a prediction of the rate of penetration and not a substitute for a bit run analysis.

sources.title: Chen, Yang and Gao, Drilling Performance Optimization Based on Mechanical Specific Energy Technologies, IntechOpen (2018): MSE as the mechanical work per unit volume of rock, Teale's MSE = WOB/Ab + 120π·RPM·T/(Ab·ROP) with WOB in lbf, T in ft·lbf, Ab in in² and ROP in ft/h, and the Pessier and Fear refinement that followed.

Menand and Mills, AADE-17-NTCE-033, Use of Mechanical Specific Energy Calculation in Real-Time to Better Detect Vibrations and Bit Wear While Drilling: the same MSE equation in psi and the caveat that MSE is driven mainly by downhole torque while the weight-on-bit term is usually neglected.
